all_public_epsilons.method: Run solve.py for P1-P5 and independently recompute each deficit, clipping, R, FOPT and FWIT from the public JSON and output; check capacity and epsilon.

auxiliary_bounds.method: Inspect built MILP variable bounds: each deficit variable has (-infinity,+infinity); each realized variable has only logical [0,max(q_i)] bounds.

R01.implementation: solve.py build(): q bounds from decision_variables.fixed/domains; model.json decision_variables

R03.implementation: solve.py build(): exact linear equalities for Q, own_i, real_i, Z

R04.implementation: solve.py build(): deficit equalities from layer1_deficit_models; absent coefficients omitted

R05.implementation: solve.py add_clip(): three binary regimes, complete implication Big-M constants computed from deficit_bounds and q domains

R06.implementation: solve.py add_pwl(): exactly one adjacent public segment for each of own2_INJECT3, Q2 and Z2

R08.implementation: solve.py build(): FOPT uses public coefficients times real_i plus Z2; FWIT uses public intercept and Z

R09.implementation: solve.py build()/main(): maximize FOPT with FWIT<=--epsilon

R10.implementation: solve.py build(): no WBHP symbol or constraint

R12.implementation: solve.py argparse --epsilon/--output and JSON audit fields

R14.implementation: solve.py reads only public JSON and solves MILP; no reference or OPM values

R15.implementation: solve.py add_clip() uses deficit_bounds only to derive M; deficit variable is unbounded; realized_bounds never used as feasibility bounds
